faqs.q: How much does wildlife removal cost in Naples?
faqs.a: Naples pricing reflects finish level: matching tile, hidden fasteners, and estate-scale rooflines take time, and canal properties add seawall and dock work. We inspect thoroughly, itemize the entries and materials in a written quote, and let the number follow the property rather than a flat rate.

faqs.q: A bear keeps raiding trash in my east Naples neighborhood — can you remove it?
faqs.a: No — black bears are excluded from Florida's nuisance-take rule; a bear is never a private trapping job. What works is removing the reward: bear-resistant trash containers, garage storage of cans until morning, no bird seed or pet food outside during bear activity, and a call to FWC's bear management program, which tracks repeat animals in Collier County. Most east Naples bear visits end within a week or two once the food disappears, and we will walk your property and point out every attractant honestly.

Naples.wildlife_intro:
Naples layers Old Naples cottages and Port Royal estates over the canal suburbs of Golden Gate's city grid and the golf communities stretching east — and a Big Cypress edge that keeps sending wildlife in. Roof rats are the aristocrats here, feasting on royal palm fruit and nesting in tile roofs from Park Shore to Pelican Bay. Burrowing owls hold protected burrows in vacant lots and even golf roughs, iguanas graze the seawalls of Naples Bay, and in the eastern communities, black bears from the Picayune occasionally work trash cans — a coexistence problem, not a trapping one.

Naples work is high-finish work: exclusion on a tile estate roof has to be invisible from the street and durable in salt air, and we spec it that way. Owl and tortoise burrows on development lots are referred to the FWC permitting track. Bears get honest advice — bear-resistant cans, no pet food outside, FWC's bear program for repeat animals — because Florida law does not make a black bear a private removal job under any reading of the nuisance rule.

faqs.q: How much does wildlife removal cost in Marco Island?
faqs.a: Marco Island quotes factor in canal-front scope — seawall, dock, and roof as one system — and seasonal timing: sealing before owners leave is planned as one complete job rather than emergency calls later. Written pricing follows the inspection, with burrow locations on the lot mapped and flagged as no-work zones in your plan.

faqs.q: Burrowing owls have a burrow in my Marco Island yard — what should I do?
faqs.a: Enjoy them, from a respectful distance. The Florida burrowing owl is State Threatened; its burrow is protected, and disturbing the birds or collapsing the burrow without an FWC permit is illegal. Keep mower and trimmer clear of the entrance, keep cats indoors near the burrow, and if you plan construction or landscaping within the burrow's zone, start with FWC's burrowing owl permitting guidance. After flooding rains owls sometimes shelter briefly under eaves — give them a day or two and they return to the burrow on their own.

Marco Island.wildlife_intro:
Marco Island is Collier's barrier-island city, a grid of canals cut into a former mangrove island, all seawalls, docks, and tile roofs. Burrowing owls are the island's famous residents — protected burrows dot vacant lots and front yards, marked with little crosses and perches — and they are the first thing newcomers must learn: observe, photograph, never disturb. The removal work is roof rats in the canal palms, raccoons on the docks, iguanas basking on seawalls, and gopher tortoises on the remaining undeveloped parcels.

Marco's owl density means any lot-level work starts with a burrow check. Iguana removal here is the same legal picture as the rest of deep-south Florida — Prohibited species, humane removal on your property, never relocated. For the many seasonal homes, we emphasize full sealing before the summer vacancy, because an empty Marco house with one open soffit becomes a rat colony by fall, discovered when the owners return to a damaged attic.

faqs.q: How much does wildlife removal cost in Immokalee?
faqs.a: Immokalee pricing is scoped per structure and per problem — a warehouse rat exclusion, a house attic, and a yard armadillo program are separate lines, quoted in writing after one combined inspection so agricultural budgets can phase the work sensibly.

faqs.q: Rats are in our Immokalee storage building — what is the process?
faqs.a: We start by removing the invitation: spilled feed and produce stored off the floor in sealed containers, vegetation cut back from the walls. Then we trap inside the structure and seal the entry points — dock-door gaps, vent screens, conduit penetrations — with gnaw-proof materials. Our portion is trapping and exclusion only; chemical rodent programs are FDACS Chapter 482 pest-control territory. With the building sealed and food secured, rat pressure in farm storage usually collapses quickly because the surrounding fields offer easier living.

Immokalee.wildlife_intro:
Immokalee is Collier's agricultural heart — tomato and citrus country, farmworker housing, packinghouses, and a growing town grid an hour inland from the coast. Wildlife work here is practical and rural: raccoons and opossums around outbuildings and dumpsters, roof rats in warehouses and homes alike, armadillos and pocket gophers in the sandy farm soils, and snakes — including the eastern diamondback in palmetto edges — around field borders. Lake Trafford, north of town, adds alligators and wading birds to the local picture.

We serve Immokalee with the same inspection-first approach as the coast, scaled to agricultural properties: multiple structures, worker housing, and storage buildings assessed in one walk, with priorities ranked by food-safety and property risk. Packing and storage rat work is nonchemical trapping and exclusion on our side; any pesticide program belongs to a Chapter 482 licensee, and we will say so plainly when a job crosses that line.

faqs.q: How much does wildlife removal cost in Golden Gate?
faqs.a: Golden Gate quotes depend first on which Golden Gate you live in. A City canal ranch is a one-structure seal; an Estates property can be a multi-building program quoted in phases. We inspect everything you want covered, write the phases separately, and never bill Estates acreage at a suburban flat assumption or vice versa.

faqs.q: A huge squirrel visits my Golden Gate Estates feeder — is it a removal candidate?
faqs.a: No, and please do not let anyone trap it. Large, slow, grizzled squirrels in this corner of Collier County can be Big Cypress fox squirrels, a State Threatened subspecies whose range includes the Estates' southern fringe — and all fox squirrels in Florida may not be taken or pursued, regardless of subspecies. Our squirrel work is eastern gray squirrels in attics, period. A fox squirrel at a feeder is a treat to watch; if one is somehow getting into a structure, the lawful answer is exclusion after it leaves, and we are glad to advise.

Golden Gate.wildlife_intro:
Golden Gate splits into two worlds: Golden Gate City, the dense canal-grid suburb built in the 1960s-80s west of the river, and Golden Gate Estates, the vast rural-residential grid of big lots and dirt roads reaching toward the Picayune Strand. The City produces canal-side roof rats, iguanas on the seawalls, and raccoons in ranch attics; the Estates produce the full rural set — bears in trash, armadillos, tortoises on the sandy lots, diamondbacks in the palmettos, and the Big Cypress fox squirrel's neighborhood to the south, where any big slow squirrel is a protected stop, not a target.

Estates properties get acreage inspections: house, well house, shed, and RV pad checked as one system, with attractant advice for bear country — cans in the garage, grills cleaned, no feeding stations. In the City, the work is canal-climate exclusion, corrosion-proof and complete. Both halves share Collier's iguana rule: removal on your property is lawful and encouraged by FWC; relocation is prohibited, always.

faqs.q: How much does wildlife removal cost in Everglades City?
faqs.a: It depends on the animal, how it got in, and how much sealing and cleanup the home needs afterward. Our crew inspects first, shows you the entry points we found, and gives you a quote after inspection before any removal or sealing work begins, with no prices promised over the phone.

faqs.q: When can bats be excluded from a Everglades City home?
faqs.a: Bat exclusion is legal in Florida from August 15 through April 15. Excluding or blocking bats during maternity season, April 16 through August 14, is illegal under FWC Rule 68A-9.010. The house bats here are Brazilian free-tailed and evening bats. In maternity season our crew can inspect, identify the roost, and schedule the exclusion for the legal window — and a bat found in a room with a sleeping person is a county health department call first.

Everglades City.wildlife_intro:
In Everglades City, our crew's steady calls are raccoons in attics and chimneys, eastern gray squirrels at soffits and gable vents, and roof rats moving from palms and fruit trees onto rooflines. Opossums and striped skunks work yards after dark, armadillos dig lawns and beds, eastern moles tunnel the sandy ground, and Brazilian free-tailed and evening bats roost in older rooflines through the warm months. The county's habitat — affluent coastal Naples, inland Immokalee farm country, and vast Everglades preserve land — and features such as Big Cypress National Preserve, Everglades National Park western edge, Fakahatchee Strand Preserve, Ten Thousand Islands keep that pressure close to housing in every season.

Florida has no winter shutdown for this work, so Everglades City jobs run year-round, with the one hard legal gate being bats: exclusion is legal only from August 15 through April 15, and maternity-season bat calls become inspection and scheduling. Our crew works under FWC Rule 68A-9.010 with the property owner's authorization — Florida issues no nuisance-trapper license — checks any live trap at least every 24 hours, and seals the entry as part of the job so the next animal cannot use the same opening. Call us at (844) 544-3498 and tell us what you are hearing or seeing.

faqs.q: How much does wildlife removal cost in Ave Maria?
faqs.a: Ave Maria quotes usually surprise owners pleasantly and then soberly: the animal count is low, but the builder-gap count is high, and sealing ten small openings is the real job. We price the gap audit and exclusion package in writing after inspection, sized to the home's phase and roof type, rather than charging per animal for a problem that is really about construction.

faqs.q: Owls are on the empty lot across from my Ave Maria house — should I report them?
faqs.a: Reporting is optional; respecting them is not. Burrowing owls on platted Ave Maria lots are State Threatened, their burrows are protected, and construction near a burrow follows FWC permitting — a fact builders here know well. For residents, the rules are simple: watch from the street, keep dogs away, and never collapse or flood a burrow. If you are buying a lot with a burrow, ask the builder how the FWC permit is being handled before closing; that paperwork is the developer's responsibility, not a wildlife company's removal job.

Ave Maria.wildlife_intro:
Ave Maria is the new town built beside its university in the Collier interior — neo-traditional neighborhoods, a town center around the oratory, and streets that still end at construction phases, preserves, and farmland. New-town wildlife is edge wildlife: raccoons and roof rats testing brand-new rooflines, armadillos digging fresh sod, burrowing owls colonizing the vacant platted lots, and sandhill cranes strolling the parks. The surrounding tomato fields and the Camp Keais Strand keep a full rural cast just past the last streetlight.

New construction is not sealed construction — builder gaps at roof returns, unsealed conduit, and open garage corners are standard finds in Ave Maria inspections, and rats find them within the first year. We specialize in that builder-gap audit here. Owl lots and crane conflicts are handled as protected-species guidance; the removal list — rats, raccoons, gray squirrels, armadillos — gets trapped and excluded with the roofline hardened so the new house stays new.
